title: BJJ Position Family Template - Hub + Bottom + Top
description: Template for position families WITH variations (Mount, Guards, etc.). Generates hub page + bottom page + top page.

hub.title: Mount Position | Complete BJJ Guide | BJJ Graph
hub.description: Master mount position in BJJ. Complete guide covering defense, attacks, and variations with 75% control retention rate.
hub.overview: Mount is one of the most dominant positions in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, representing complete positional control where the top practitioner sits astride the opponent's torso. Worth 4 points in IBJJF competition, mount provides the top player with numerous submission opportunities while the bottom player faces limited escape options. The position exemplifies the fundamental BJJ principle of using superior positioning to overcome size and strength advantages. Advanced practitioners retain mount 85% of the time and finish submissions in 65% of exchanges. (400+ words minimum)
key_principles: Maintain low center of gravity with hips on opponent's chest
Control opponent's arms to prevent bridging and escape attempts
Distribute weight through hips, not hands, for maximum pressure

variations.name: High Mount
variations.description: Knees positioned on shoulders for maximum control and submission options

variations.name: S-Mount
variations.description: Asymmetric position setting up armbar and triangle attacks

variations.name: Technical Mount
variations.description: Position used for back take and maintaining control when opponent turns

metadata.title: Mount Bottom (Defense) | BJJ Position Guide | BJJ Graph
metadata.description: Master mount escapes and defensive strategies. Complete guide to surviving mount, creating frames, and executing high-percentage escapes with 55% advanced success rate.

bottom.overview: Being mounted is one of the worst positions in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, but with proper defensive technique and systematic escapes, even beginners can recover to neutral or better positions. The key to mount defense lies in creating frames immediately to prevent the top player from consolidating control, maintaining defensive posture to protect against submissions, and executing high-percentage escapes at the right moments. Understanding the biomechanics of escape creates opportunities to reverse the dominant position. (400+ words minimum)
state_invariants: Bottom player flat on back with top player sitting on torso with direct weight distribution
Top player's knees on either side of bottom player's ribs, eliminating escape space
Bottom player attempting to create frames and defensive space to prevent flattening
prerequisites: Recognition of submission threats and defensive priorities
Ability to bridge explosively when opponent overcommits
Foot positioning awareness for trap-and-roll setups
key_principles: Create frames immediately to prevent flattening and maintain breathing space
Keep elbows tight to body to prevent arm attacks and isolations
Trap opponent's foot when possible to set up elbow escape
Bridge explosively when opponent overcommits forward or posts hands
Protect neck from chokes at all times with defensive hand positioning
Use hip movement (shrimping) to create angles for escape
Never push directly on opponent's chest (exposes arms to attacks)

counter_transitions.trigger: When opponent attempts cross choke, use frames to create space
When opponent goes for armbar, turn into them and recover half guard
When opponent breaks frames, immediately re-establish defensive structure

decision_tree.condition: If opponent is high mounted with chest near your face
If opponent maintains low base with distributed weight
If opponent posts hands for submission attempt

common_errors.error: Pushing directly on opponent's chest or face with straight arms
common_errors.consequence: Exposes arms to attacks, wastes energy, and gives opponent armbar opportunities
common_errors.correction: Create frames on hips and knees instead, keeping elbows tight to body

common_errors.error: Remaining flat on back without creating frames
common_errors.consequence: Allows opponent to consolidate position and reduces breathing capacity
common_errors.correction: Immediately establish defensive frames and create space for hip movement

common_errors.error: Attempting escapes without first controlling opponent's weight
common_errors.consequence: Wasted energy and increased submission vulnerability
common_errors.correction: Use frames to manipulate opponent's balance before attempting escapes

common_errors.error: Bridging without trapping opponent's foot or arm
common_errors.consequence: Opponent easily posts and maintains position
common_errors.correction: Always trap at least one limb before executing bridge-based escapes

common_errors.error: Giving up arms when attempting to turn or escape
common_errors.consequence: Immediate submission via armbar or kimura
common_errors.correction: Keep arms protected and use hip movement rather than arm extension

training_drills.name: Mount Retention Drill
training_drills.description: Partner holds mount while you practice creating frames and recovering guard. Focus on hip movement and frame positioning. Duration: 2-3 minutes per round.

training_drills.name: Elbow Escape Repetitions
training_drills.description: Starting from mount bottom, practice shrimping motion and knee insertion for half guard recovery. 10-15 repetitions per side.

training_drills.name: Upa Escape Timing Drill
training_drills.description: Partner maintains mount and posts hands periodically. Practice recognizing the moment and executing explosive bridge. Focus on timing over strength.

optimal_submission_paths.name: Survival to Guard Recovery
optimal_submission_paths.path: Mount Bottom → Create Frames → Trap Foot → Elbow Escape → Half Guard → Guard Recovery

optimal_submission_paths.name: Emergency Reversal
optimal_submission_paths.path: Mount Bottom → Recognize Overcommitment → Upa Escape → Mount Top → Consolidate Position

optimal_submission_paths.name: Progressive Escape Chain
optimal_submission_paths.path: Mount Bottom → Frame Creation → Hip Escape → Half Guard → Butterfly Sweep → Top Position

retention_rate.description: Percentage of time position is maintained when under attack

advancement_probability.description: Probability of successfully escaping to better position

submission_probability.description: Probability of finishing from this position (bottom player rarely submits from mount)

position_metrics.average_time: 45-90 seconds (beginner holds longer due to limited escape knowledge)

expert_insights.danaher: The mount escape is fundamentally about creating the space necessary to insert your frames and generate the angular momentum required for hip escape. The beginner's mistake is pushing against immovable pressure rather than redirecting it. Focus on creating angles through shrimping motion and using opponent's forward pressure against them through bridging mechanics.
expert_insights.gordon_ryan: In competition, I find the elbow escape to be the highest percentage option because it doesn't require explosive power and works even against heavy pressure. The key is timing the escape when your opponent shifts weight to attack. Never wait passively - constant frame pressure forces them to make decisions that create escape opportunities.
expert_insights.eddie_bravo: From mount bottom, the Lockdown system provides an alternative path that many traditional practitioners overlook. Once you get to half guard via the elbow escape, immediately establish the lockdown to control their base and set up the Old School sweep. This turns a defensive disaster into an offensive opportunity.

metadata.title: Mount Top (Attacks) | BJJ Position Guide | BJJ Graph
metadata.description: Master mount attacks and submissions. Complete guide to maintaining mount, breaking posture, and finishing with 75% control retention rate and 65% submission probability.

top.overview: Mount top is the pinnacle of positional control in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, offering the top player maximum offensive opportunities while minimizing defensive requirements. The position provides access to numerous high-percentage submissions including chokes, armbars, and shoulder locks, while the stable base allows for sustained pressure and control. Mastering mount requires balancing submission attacks with positional maintenance, understanding when to attack and when to consolidate. (400+ words minimum)
state_invariants: Top player sitting on opponent's torso with knees tight to ribs for maximum control
Weight distributed through hips onto opponent's diaphragm, limiting breathing and movement
Hands free for attacks while maintaining stable base through hip and knee positioning
prerequisites: Successful guard pass or transition from side control
Understanding of weight distribution for pressure control
Recognition of submission opportunities and setups
Ability to maintain base while executing attacks
Knowledge of countering common escape attempts
key_principles: Keep knees tight to opponent's armpits to prevent escape space
Sink hips into opponent's chest for maximum pressure and control
Distribute weight through hips, not hands, to keep hands free for attacks
Maintain low center of gravity to prevent bridging escapes
Follow opponent's movement and maintain position before attacking
Use submission attempts as position advancement opportunities
Stay heavy and pressure-focused while attacking

counter_transitions.trigger: When opponent attempts elbow escape, shift to S-mount and attack arm
When opponent turns to side during escape attempt, follow and take technical mount
When opponent creates strong frames, walk knees higher for increased control
When opponent bridges, post hand and swing leg over for armbar
When opponent turns away from attack, secure gift wrap and take the back

decision_tree.condition: If opponent creates strong frames and begins elbow escape
If opponent remains defensive with arms protecting chest
If opponent exposes arms while attempting escape
If opponent turns to side during defense

common_errors.error: Posting hands on mat for base during attacks
common_errors.consequence: Allows opponent to trap arm and execute upa escape or arm attacks
common_errors.correction: Keep hands high and ready for attacks, base through hips and distribute weight correctly

common_errors.error: Rising up too high when attempting submissions
common_errors.consequence: Creates space for opponent to shrimp and escape, reduces control
common_errors.correction: Maintain low chest position and use weight to break posture before attacking

common_errors.error: Attacking too early without controlling opponent's arms
common_errors.consequence: Opponent frames and creates escape opportunities
common_errors.correction: Establish control of arms and posture before transitioning to submissions

common_errors.error: Remaining static and not responding to escape attempts
common_errors.consequence: Opponent successfully escapes to half guard or guard
common_errors.correction: Follow opponent's movement and transition to S-mount or technical mount

common_errors.error: Using all strength for submission without technical setup
common_errors.consequence: Exhaustion and creating escape opportunities through muscling
common_errors.correction: Use proper mechanics and weight distribution to create submission pressure

training_drills.name: Mount Maintenance Drill
training_drills.description: Partner attempts various escapes while you maintain position for 2-3 minutes. Focus on weight distribution and following movement rather than attacking. Build positional awareness.

training_drills.name: Submission Chain Drill
training_drills.description: Practice flowing between americana, armbar, and cross choke based on partner's defensive reactions. Focus on smooth transitions and maintaining pressure throughout.

training_drills.name: Transition to Advanced Positions
training_drills.description: Starting from standard mount, practice recognizing escape attempts and transitioning to S-mount, high mount, and technical mount. Partner provides realistic resistance.

position_metrics.average_time: 1-3 minutes (depends on top player's submission awareness and opponent's defensive skills)

expert_insights.danaher: Mount control requires constant pressure adjustment based on opponent's defensive movements. The fundamental principle is maintaining your center of gravity over their center of mass while keeping your base wide and low. Don't rush submissions - the position itself creates fatigue and opens opportunities. Use systematic breaking of defensive structures before attempting finishes.
expert_insights.gordon_ryan: I prefer the cross choke from mount because it's high percentage and doesn't require giving up position. The key is using your body weight to break their posture first, then establishing the first grip deep. Most people try to finish too quickly - take your time, control their head with your chest, and methodically set up the second grip. The submission becomes inevitable.
expert_insights.eddie_bravo: From mount top, the gift wrap position opens up the entire 10th Planet system of back attacks. When they turn away from your attack, immediately secure the gift wrap and transition to technical mount or the back. This creates a dilemma - defend the submission and give up the back, or defend the back and get submitted from mount. That's fundamental 10P strategy.
